rounds.text: Kesar Terminals & Infrastructure Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading deep in value territory with a price-to-book ratio of -0.76x against a sector benchmark of 1.39x [E1, E6]. Despite sitting at just 15% of its 52-week range [E4], the underlying business exhibits extraordinary capital efficiency, generating an elite ROCE of 92.55% and an ROE of 31.22%, both crushing sector benchmarks of 6.61% and 5.09% respectively [E8, E9]. Furthermore, the company trades at a highly attractive EV/EBITDA of 3.89x compared to the sector benchmark of 10.49x [E10], while rewarding shareholders with a 2.85% dividend yield [E3]. Operational execution is exceptionally cash-generative, demonstrated by a stellar cash conversion rate of 1.24x, operating cash flow of Rs 9.94 Cr, and free cash flow of Rs 9.71 Cr for March 2025 where profits were 98% backed by cash [E26, E27, E28, E29]. Recent momentum also signals a sharp inflection, highlighted by a powerful 47% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and 14% top-line growth [E14, E17], alongside positive signals that profit growth is beginning to exceed 1-year price growth by 86% as the company starts outperforming expectations [E37]. Conceded: [E11], [E12], [E13], [E15], [E18], [E21], [E22], [E23], [E30], [E31], [E39], [E40], [E41], [E42], [E43], [E45], [E46].

Kesar Terminals & Infrastructure Ltd carries profound balance sheet and margin risks that undermine its headline profitability metrics. The current ratio sits at an alarming 0.06x as current liabilities heavily exceed current assets, compounded by rising borrowings of Rs 91.95 Cr and a flagged low interest coverage ratio alongside high borrowing costs [E30, E31, E39, E43]. Furthermore, structural top-line contraction is entrenched, demonstrated by negative compounded sales growth over 10 years (-2%), 5 years (-3%), and 3 years (-5%), alongside official flags for poor historical sales growth [E11, E12, E13, E40]. Margins are aggressively deteriorating, with quarterly operating margins collapsing by 31 percentage points to 11% in June 2025 and trailing twelve-month margins contracting by 12 percentage points [E22, E23]. Earnings quality is severely compromised by a massive Rs 29.9 Cr component of other income included in earnings, alongside looming contingent liabilities of Rs 128 Cr [E41, E42]. Compounded share price performance reflects this underlying weakness, down 39% over the past year and 13% over a decade, with the rules-based screen scoring a mediocre 44 out of 100 driven by decelerating earnings growth and a steep 89% year-over-year drop in net profit [E18, E21, E44, E45, E46]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong short-term cash conversion at 1.24x with robust operating cash flow and high ROCE of 92.55% [E9, E26].

Conceded: current liabilities exceed current assets at a current ratio of 0.06x, borrowings stand at Rs 91.95 Cr, and there are warning flags for low interest coverage, high borrowing costs, contingent liabilities of Rs 128 Cr, and other income of Rs 29.9 Cr [E30, E31, E39, E41, E42, E43]. Conceded: compounded sales growth has been negative over 10, 5, and 3 years, margins have dropped in the trailing twelve months and June 2025, and historical share price performance shows declines over 1 and 10 years alongside a 44/100 screen score [E11, E12, E13, E18, E21, E22, E23, E40, E44, E45, E46]. However, these structural challenges obscure exceptional capital efficiency, evidenced by a phenomenal ROCE of 92.55% that towers over the sector benchmark of 6.61% [E9]. Furthermore, the business is exceptionally cash-generative despite its headwinds, delivering Rs 9.94 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 9.71 Cr in free cash flow for March 2025, with a cash conversion ratio of 1.24x proving that profits are fully backed by cash [E26, E27, E28, E29]. Near-term momentum and fundamental reality have also started shifting positively, as demonstrated by a 14% bounce in trailing twelve-month sales growth and a 47% surge in compounded profit growth [E14, E17]. Finally, the market price has already heavily penalized the stock, leaving it sitting at just 15% of its 52-week range and offering a 2.85% dividend yield while the company outperforms recent expectations [E3, E4, E37].

Conceded: the company delivered operating and free cash flows of Rs 9.94 Cr and Rs 9.71 Cr respectively alongside a 1.24x cash conversion ratio in March 2025 [E26, E27, E28, E29], and sits at 15% of its 52-week range offering a 2.85% dividend yield [E3, E4]. However, that supposed exceptional capital efficiency is severely undermined by a negative return on assets of -0.42% against the sector benchmark of 2.86% [E7], and an alarming current ratio of just 0.06x where current liabilities heavily swamp current assets [E30]. Furthermore, the cited ROCE of 92.55% [E9] loses validity when weighed against flashing danger signs of a low interest coverage ratio, high borrowing costs, rising borrowings to Rs 91.95 Cr, and massive contingent liabilities of Rs 128 Cr [E31, E39, E41, E43]. The argument that fundamentals are shifting positively through trailing sales and profit bounces [E14, E17] completely ignores a multi-year secular decay featuring negative 10, 5, and 3-year sales growth [E11, E12, E13] and an ugly 89% year-over-year net profit collapse flagged by the screen [E45]. Finally, relying on TTM metrics masks severe operational deterioration, as evidenced by quarterly operating margins plunging by 31 percentage points down to 11% in June 2025 [E23] and earnings that are suspiciously propped up by Rs 29.9 Cr of other income [E42].
